subject.title: Crons ejecutaron mensajes de WhatsApp a la 1 AM fuera de horario y no se podían detener

question: Should this issue be resolved by landing the schedule-activation replay fix first and tracking emergency stop/delete semantics separately, or should one combined change define cron remove/gateway stop as an emergency outbound-delivery halt?
rationale: The replay bug has a concrete candidate implementation, but the requested stop/delete behavior changes user-visible operator semantics across cron, gateway lifecycle, task cancellation, and channel delivery.

options.title: Land Replay Fix, Split Emergency Stop
options.body: Accept the schedule-activation boundary through the existing PR or an equivalent replacement, then sponsor a separate product-scoped emergency stop design.

options.title: Require One Combined Fix
options.body: Keep this issue open until a single implementation covers restart replay, cron remove cancellation, and gateway emergency outbound halt behavior.

options.title: Narrow To Replay Only
options.body: Treat stop/delete and emergency halt as out of scope here and close only after the replay fix lands.

recommendation.title: Land Replay Fix, Split Emergency Stop
recommendation.body: Accept the schedule-activation boundary through the existing PR or an equivalent replacement, then sponsor a separate product-scoped emergency stop design.

likelyOwner.reason: This person already provided land-ready verification for the active replay-fix PR and is the clearest owner for the remaining persisted-state/product-boundary choice.
